q: In the labelled transverse section of the thorax at the level of the heart shown below, match each numbered structure (1–4) with the appropriate anatomical or clinical description: 1. Undergoes hypertrophy on pulmonary stenosis 2. Receives oxygenated blood 3. Arises from left ventricle 4. Lies to the right of ascending aorta (Q-18718823)
o: 1-Undergoes hypertrophy on pulmonary stenosis, 2-Receives oxygenated blood, 3-Arises from left ventricle, 4- Lies to the right of ascending aorta
1-Receives oxygenated blood, 2- Undergoes hypertrophy on pulmonary stenosis, 3-Arises from left ventricle, 4- Lies to the right of ascending aorta
1-Receives oxygenated blood, 2- Undergoes hypertrophy on pulmonary stenosis, 3- Lies to the right of ascending aorta, 4-Arises from left ventricle
1-Receives oxygenated blood, 2- Arises from left ventricle, 3- Lies to the right of ascending aorta, 4-Undergoes hypertrophy on pulmonary stenosis

q: A 29-year-old woman with a pituitary microadenoma has been receiving cabergoline 1 mg per week. She presents at 12 weeks of gestation. What is the most appropriate management? (Q-39909950)
o: Advise termination of pregnancy as cabergoline was continued during the first trimester
Follow up with serum prolactin levels monthly
Perform MRI of the sella to look for tumor enlargement
Reassure the patient and evaluate further only if symptoms such as headache or visual disturbance develop

q: A 65-year-old patient with a history of coronary artery disease is prescribed clopidogrel (Plavix) and omeprazole (Prilosec) for concurrent use. Which of the following statements regarding this drug combination is most accurate? (Q-55031530)
o: The combination of clopidogrel and omeprazole is safe and does not require any monitoring
Omeprazole may enhance the antiplatelet effects of clopidogrel, leading to improved cardiovascular outcomes and increasing the risk of cardiovascular events
Omeprazole inhibits the activity of CYP2C19, potentially reducing the effectiveness of clopidogrel
Clopidogrel increases the metabolism of omeprazole, leading to decreased therapeutic levels of omeprazole in the body

q: A patient undergoing antitubercular therapy reports joint pain 10 days after initiation of treatment. Laboratory tests reveal normal AST and ALT levels, a serum creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL, and an elevated serum uric acid level of 10 mg/dL. What is the most appropriate next step in managing this patient's treatment? (Q-54340846)
o: Stop pyrazinamide and continue the rest of the drugs with kidney function test (KFT) monitoring.
Add uric acid-lowering drugs and continue antitubercular therapy (ATT) as such with liver function test (LFT) and KFT monitoring.
Continue all drugs and monitor serum uric acid level as well as LFT and KFT.
Stop all ATT drugs until laboratory values return to normal.

q: A 28-year-old G5L4 with all 4-girl children presents at 18 weeks and asks for the sex of the child on ultrasound. This is her first antenatal visit. What should be done? (Q-87012106)
o: Do ultrasound for gestational age, check for abnormalities, check sex, and tell the mother
Do ultrasound for gestational age, check for abnormalities, check sex but don’t tell the mother
Do ultrasound for gestational age, check for abnormalities, don’t check the sex or reveal to the mother
Don’t do ultrasound, do ANC only

q: A 43-year-old man is being evaluated for suspected lymphoma-related obstruction of the lymphatic system. The radiology team plans to perform pedal lymphangiography. Which of the following best describes how this procedure is performed? (Q-20788289)
o: The lymphatic channels on the dorsum of the foot are cannulated after injecting a blue dye, and an oily contrast agent is slowly infused to opacify the lymphatic system.
A peripheral intravenous line is placed in the dorsal venous arch and water-soluble contrast is rapidly injected to visualize lymphatics under fluoroscopy.
A CT-guided direct puncture of para-aortic lymph nodes is performed and contrast medium is infused retrogradely.
A radionuclide-labeled tracer is injected subcutaneously and lymphatic drainage is evaluated with a gamma camera.
